question: In the case of a convex mirror, a ray parallel to the principal axis after reflection appears to diverge from:
solution:
The correct answer is __**The principal focus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• In a **convex mirror**, the reflected rays of light appear to diverge from a single point located behind the mirror. This point is called the **principal focus**.
 
• A ray parallel to the principal axis of a convex mirror, after reflection, appears to originate from the **principal focus**. This is a fundamental property of convex mirrors.
 
• The principal focus of a convex mirror is a **virtual point** because the reflected rays do not actually converge but appear to diverge from this point when extended backward.
 
• The principal focus lies on the mirror's principal axis at a distance equal to half the radius of curvature (i.e., the focal length, **f**, is **R/2**).
